headline: Low prompt-injection and data-conflict risk; no direct shared-channel pathway is documented, but Whisper’s file-based CLI can still ingest attacker-controlled audio content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a docs-only prompt-leak repository with no runnable I/O, while agent B (Whisper) processes audio files via command-line usage. There is no documented shared channel between them, so direct injection is not established; the only plausible bridge is manual handoff of content, which is low blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A-derived text into B’s transcription workflow, then prompt-like content can influence downstream handling.
IF B is wrapped by a parser that treats transcribed text as instructions, then attacker-controlled audio can steer outputs.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Review transcriptions before any downstream use.
Disable any automation that interprets transcripts as commands.
Use a fixed prompt template for B outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from audio source to transcript consumers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network surfaces; B touches audio/speech and reads audio files, but its network egress is none and it has no filesystem write. With no shared workspace or outbound upload path documented, leakage risk is limited to local handling of audio files.
conditions: IF A is placed in the same directory as sensitive audio files consumed by B, then B can process those files locally.
IF an external wrapper exports B’s transcripts elsewhere, then audio-derived content may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Store sensitive audio in a separate directory.
Run B only on non-sensitive samples.
Delete temporary transcripts after review.
Confirm no wrapper uploads transcripts.
requires-engineering: enforce per-job workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or mutable-resource capabilities documented, and B explicitly lacks filesystem write, git modification, subprocess spawning, and multiple-instance support. There is no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource in the profiles, so a capability conflict pathway is not plausible.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, then conflict risk would change.
IF future tooling adds shared mutable state, then coordination would be required.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid shared writable directories.
Do not enable git automation around either agent.
Use one-job-at-a-time scheduling.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can consume audio files and produce transcripts, but A is a source-available leak repository with no runnable output or action-taking authority. There is no documented pipeline where B treats A’s output as authoritative, so cascading error is limited to manual misuse rather than a default chain.
conditions: IF an operator feeds A-derived text into B as reference material, then transcription quality may be biased.
IF B’s transcript is used by another system without review, then downstream errors can propagate.
mitigations: Do not use A as ground truth.
Manually verify transcripts before reuse.
Separate source material from evaluation material.
Flag uncertain segments for review.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented. A has no data classes touched and B only touches audio/speech with local command-line usage and no network egress, so the profiles do not show a compliance-violating data flow.
conditions: IF future deployment routes audio or transcripts to a regulated third party, then compliance review is needed.
IF either agent is repurposed for PHI or EU PII, then residency and retention controls must be rechecked.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Document retention for any transcripts.
Review deployment region before use.
Avoid third-party transcription relays.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
